# Introduction
> Estimate the difference in weight change between quitters and non-quitters, and its uncertainty, in situations where the standard formulas either don’t exist or might not be appropriate. 

This report uses bootstrapping to estimate the uncertainty associated with differences in weight change between participants who quit smoking and those who continued smoking. The analysis uses data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Epidemiologic Follow-up Study (NHEFS), which followed participants between 1971 and 1982. The outcome of interest is weight change (kg) over this period, while the exposure is smoking cessation status (quitters versus non-quitters). Bootstrapping is used to estimate the standard errors and confidence intervals for the difference in median weight change and to assess uncertainty in covariate-adjusted linear regression estimates.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-groups
#| tbl-cap: "Median weight change (kg) by smoking status"

tab <- data.frame(
  Group = c("Quit smoking", "Continued smoking", "Total"),
  n = c(n_quit, n_cont, n_total),
  `Median weight change (kg)` = c(round(med_quit, 2), round(med_cont, 2), NA),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(tab, align = "lrr", na = "")
```
